proofs.full_local_argument: For constant positive multiplier k^2, the Levi-Civita connection is unchanged: in the Christoffel formula the inverse metric contributes k^-2 and every metric derivative contributes k^2. Thus affine geodesics, exp_x on tangent vectors and log_x as a tangent vector are unchanged. Lengths and distances multiply by k, and sectional curvature divides by k^2, giving curvature -1. Consequently the same geodesic convexity inequalities hold, |f(x)-f(y)|<=L d_g(x,y)=(L/k)d_{g'}(x,y), and the ball of radius r becomes the ball of radius R=kr with the same open/closed convention. For every tangent h, set h'=h/k^2. Then <h',log_x y>_{g'}=k^2<h/k^2,log_x y>_g=<h,log_x y>_g. Therefore the global support inequality holds for h exactly when it holds for h'; the inverse is h=k^2h'. Norms satisfy ||h'||_{g'}=||h||_g/k. This is a pointwise bijection of full subdifferentials, hence also of fixed selections, including repeated queries. A simulator uses identical physical queries, returns the unchanged value and converts the selected vector as above; the reverse simulator multiplies by k^2. Each conversion uses no objective call, preserves deterministic histories and outputs, and preserves nonreturn or budget excess. The objective minimum and gap are unchanged, and (L/k)(kr)=Lr. Apply the linked curvature -1 Theorem at R=kr and L'=L/k to obtain the stated closed/open bounds.
map: Constant scaling preserves the connection and geodesics while scaling distances and curvature.

assumptions: f is globally geodesically convex and globally L-Lipschitz for g, with a global minimizer in the closed ball of radius r around o; open-ball localization is preserved as well.
The Oracle is exact value plus a fixed globally supporting Riemannian tangent subgradient.
Algorithms know the geometry and scaling and may perform the exact conversions without objective calls.
statement.conclusion: The g' curvature is -1; d_{g'}=k d_g; the function class and legal fixed Oracle maps correspond bijectively; epsilon L'R=epsilon Lr and query counts are unchanged. With rho=kr and zeta=rho/tanh rho, the dimension-uniform deterministic closed-ball complexity lies between zeta/(260epsilon^2) and ceil(3zeta/epsilon^2). The open-ball lower constant is 3zeta/(1040epsilon^2), with the same upper bound.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let (H^d,g) have constant sectional curvature -k^2, k>0, distance d_g and known center o. Define g'=k^2g, R=kr and L'=L/k. Keep the same real-valued objective f and physical points; map each selected tangent subgradient h to h'=h/k^2.
statement.parameter_domains: k,r,L>0. The model equivalence holds for epsilon>0; the transferred matching theorem uses 0<epsilon<=1/64.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every d>=2, k,r,L>0 and every such f and fixed Oracle selection, the transformation is invertible and gives exact query-by-query simulations. It preserves deterministic algorithms and their budget/output guarantees.
